title: BAGNet: A Boundary-Aware Graph Neural Network for SRAM Yield Analysis in Post-LayoutSimulation
problem: Post-layout SRAM yield analysis is complicated by inter-column correlations from parasitic parameters that previous pre-layout methods ignore, making yield estimation difficult and time-consuming.
motivation: Accurate, fast yield estimation for large SRAM arrays requires models that capture post-layout effects including parasitic-induced correlations.
method: BAGNet uses a GNN to learn graph representations of SRAM arrays and generate feature vectors, constructs an MLP-based surrogate model for performance prediction, and introduces nonlinear mapping with adaptive iteration for boundary-aware capability. Uses importance sampling on the surrogate model for efficient yield estimation without circuit simulation.
key_novelty: Boundary-aware GNN-based surrogate model for SRAM yield that captures post-layout parasitic effects.
contributions: GNN-based learning of SRAM array graph representations
Nonlinear mapping strategy with adaptive iteration for boundary detection
Importance sampling-based yield estimation on surrogate model
1.82-3.52× speedup over state-of-the-art methods without accuracy loss
limitations: Evaluation limited to SRAM arrays; applicability to other memory structures not addressed.
primary_theme: GNN-based surrogate modeling for SRAM yield prediction
